newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli-Arab violence erupts in Hebron, Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-Arab violence erupts in Hebron, Gaza.

text.p: Israeli troops firing rubber bullets and live ammunition wounded eight Palestinians hurling stones and firebombs in a fresh round of violence in the West Bank town of Hebron on Wednesday.
In the self-ruled Gaza Strip, Israeli troops shot dead a Palestinian teenager during demonstrations near a strip of disputed land beside a Jewish settlement bloc, witnesses said.

Israeli snipers deployed across rooftops and alleyways along the dividing line between Israeli-and PLO-controlled sectors of Hebron, which observed a general strike called to protest anti-Moslem posters depicting the Prophet Mohammed as a pig.
Hospital sources said they treated three Palestinians who were shot in the legs with live bullets. They said five others were hit by rubber-coated metal bullets.

"Where is Hitler? Where is Yahya Ayyash?" shouted protesters, referring to Nazi leader Adolf Hitler, who led the Holocaust of Europe's Jews and a slain Palestinian bombmaker who engineered suicide attacks inside Israel.
U.S. Consul-General Edward Abington and Palestinian West Bank Preventive Security Chief Jibril Rajoub made their way towards the confrontation line in a bid to calm tensions.
"I came to see what the situation is like. I hope the tension will be reduced...by having restraint by both sides," Abington told reporters.

Palestinian police did not intervene to halt the unrest. Police sources said they feared demonstrators would use them as a protective shield, drawing fire in their direction, which could worsen the unrest.

Dozens of youths took to the streets and rained stones and petrol bombs on Israeli troops. One soldier's uniform caught on fire when a bomb landed at his feet. Witnesses said a pair of firebombs exploded near an area where foreign press gathered to watch the clashes.

In a deserted home behind the confrontation lines, dozens of Palestinians running a makeshift assembly line funneled petrol stored in a large bin into empty cola bottles and topped them off with a bit of cloth.
Teenagers lit the homemade molotov cocktails and ferried them to the frontlines to be hurled at Israeli troops.
Witnesses said Israeli bulldozers worked during the night, shovelling bricks to block entrances to the 20-metre (yard) long alley in the Israeli-controlled section of the divided town.
Israeli police are holding a 25-year-old Jewish woman suspected of pasting posters on Hebron storefronts picturing a pig in Arab headdress with the word Mohammad written on it.
The pig was portrayed stomping with one foot on the Moslem holy book, the Koran, while holding a pen in the other. Islam and Judaism regard pigs as unclean and ban the eating of pork.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the posters -- the latest spark to ignite violence in volatile Hebron.
In Gaza, dozens of Palestinians demonstrated near the Gush Qatif settlement bloc after Jewish settlers began work on a strip of land Arabs said belonged to Palestinians.
Troops opened fire with bullets and stun grenades to disperse the protesters, wounding one in the chest.
Witnesses said Israeli soldiers and Palestinian police had dug in opposite one another near the area.
"The situation is very bad and the Israeli army is behaving as if this is an Israeli military base," Khaled Abu Leila, Palestinian military liaison chief in Gaza, told Reuters.
Jewish settlers said in a statement the land belonged to Jews and accused Palestinians of attempting to seize it.

Israeli troops have clashed with Palestinian protesters almost daily since Israel's groundbreaking of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last March plunged peacemaking with the PLO into crisis.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO-rule in January but troops stayed on to guard 400 Jewish settlers who live in fortified enclaves in the heart of the city revered by Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.
